claims.text: The driver's own 'arrived' tap at 10:41:10 was false: the trip record shows the free waiting period of 180 seconds started at 10:41:12, but the GPS trace shows the driver's first qualifying in-geofence fix only at 10:43:10, and the driver's dwell inside the arrival radius lasted just 150 seconds before he cancelled at 10:45:43. The waiting clock must be recomputed from the first qualifying in-geofence fix under POL-NS-05, and on that recomputed basis the corrected dwell is 30 seconds short of the 180 second free waiting period in force for this trip.

The effective in-geofence dwell is 150 seconds against a required minimum of 180 seconds for a STANDARD zone class - a shortfall of 30 seconds. Under POL-NS-06 the cancellation fee is not chargeable and is refunded to the rider in full, whether or not the rider was present and whether or not the rider responded to messages. The fare breakdown shows the rider was charged SGD 4.50 with no refund issued.

The driver's own statement concedes the false marker: 'I pressed arrived a bit early but I did wait at the pin.' That admission, read with the GPS trace placing the first qualifying in-geofence fix at 10:43:10 - nearly two minutes after the 10:41:10 arrival tap - confirms the arrival marker was false and did not start the waiting clock.

The rider's claim that the app said the driver arrived while he was still far away is corroborated by the driver's track: the driver's mean distance from the pickup pin across the trace is 2,647 metres and his maximum distance is 7,088 metres, with distinct speeds up to 47 kph - he was travelling on the road network, not holding position at the pin, at the moment the arrival marker fired.

The rider was present at the pickup: the rider's track shows 46 fixes with a mean distance of 739 metres from the pin and a minimum of 735 metres, all at zero speed, across the window from 10:39:29 to 10:46:19. The rider's device was stationary and recording throughout the waiting window, so the rider was not the cause of the failed pickup.

The driver's chat message 'im at the pickup point' was sent at 10:41:30, twenty seconds after the false arrival tap, and the driver then cancelled at 10:45:43 without the in-geofence dwell ever reaching the required minimum. The message does not cure the shortfall: POL-NS-06 makes the refund mandatory on a short dwell regardless of the rider's response.

No traffic advisory covers this pickup road: the advisory artifact is MISSING with weight 0.0, so the limb (i) accumulation route under POL-NS-06 is unavailable and the driver cannot sum separate in-geofence intervals to reach the minimum. The single in-geofence interval of 150 seconds stands as the whole dwell.

The fare breakdown reconciles to the platform's own figure: the cancellation fee line of SGD 4.50 matches platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd, so there is no integrity defect under POL-NS-08(d) and the amount to be refunded is the full SGD 4.50 charged to the rider.

The driver's profile shows one no-show termination in the trailing 30 days against 129 completed trips - a rate of 0.008, far below the 0.08 threshold - so the POL-NS-07 anti-farming check does not trip and the case does not escalate on that ground. The rider's profile shows zero no-show disputes in 30 days and zero disputes with this counterparty in 90 days, so POL-NS-09(c) and (d) are not engaged either.

claims.text: The trip record shows a driver 'arrived' event at 10:41:10 and a wait timer started at 10:41:12, and the driver terminated the trip at 10:45:43 under reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW — the reason code POL-NS-01(d) recognises. The driver's own statement ('I pressed arrived a bit early but I did wait at the pin') is an admission only of an early marker, not of a failure to wait, and the record shows he waited 4.5 minutes before cancelling.

The driver's trace places him stationary inside the pickup geofence for a continuous qualifying run of 150 seconds, from 10:43:10 to 10:45:40, with 16 qualifying fixes — a real, sustained hold at the pin, not a drive-by. That is the dwell POL-NS-01(c) measures, and it is measured from the first qualifying in-geofence fix, exactly as the clause directs.

The rider's own device track is present and places the rider 735 to 743 metres from the pickup pin for the whole window, with 46 fixes and a single distinct speed of 0.0 kph — the rider was stationary and nowhere near the pin. The rider's claim that the driver 'was still far away on the main road' is contradicted by the rider's own telemetry: it is the rider who was far away.

The rider never sent a single locating or coordinating message. The chat log holds exactly one message, sent by the DRIVER at 10:41:30 ('im at the pickup point'), read by the rider at 10:42:00. POL-NS-04 requires a rider message during the waiting window as limb (a); there is none, so the rider-exonerating clause cannot fire on this record.

The rider's presence test under POL-NS-04(c) is affirmatively failed, not merely undecidable: the rider track is present, carries 46 fixes, and every one of them sits roughly 740 m from the pin — far outside the 100 m STANDARD rider-presence radius. POL-NS-11 only rescues a rider when the test cannot be run; here it can be run and it fails.

The rider's cancellation-fee challenge is not supported by the fare ledger: the fee charged is SGD 4.50, which reconciles exactly with platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd of 4.50 for this trip, and the ledger shows payment_status CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd 0.00. There is no integrity defect under POL-NS-08(d) for the rider to exploit.

The driver is entitled to compensation at 80 percent of the fee in force: 80 percent of SGD 4.50 is SGD 3.60, the figure the fare ledger itself computes as driver_compensation under POL-NS-07. The anti-farming check does not trip — driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 1, below the threshold of 4, and 1/129 is far below the 0.08 rate — so compensation is payable and the fee stands.

I concede the arrival marker was pressed early: the driver's own statement says so, and the trace shows the marker at 10:41:10 while the first qualifying in-geofence fix is at 10:43:10. But POL-NS-05(iii) is explicit that a false marker does not by itself defeat the fee where the corrected dwell still meets the minimum, and the corrected dwell here is 150 seconds against a STANDARD minimum of 180 seconds — so this concession is real and it costs the driver the fee.

The shortfall is 30 seconds and it is fatal to the charge. POL-NS-06 makes the waiting period strict liability: where the effective in-geofence dwell is shorter than the free waiting period in force, the fee is refunded in full whether or not the rider was present and whether or not the rider responded. The only route to accumulate dwell across intervals is POL-NS-06(i), and it is unavailable here — the trace shows a single in-geofence interval, and the traffic advisory artifact is MISSING, which the policy says makes limb (i) unavailable rather than exonerating anyone.

The rider's own conduct record does not support a finding of abuse against the driver: rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 0 and rider_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d is 0, so the POL-NS-09(d) and POL-NS-09(c) escalation triggers do not fire. I note rider_profile.prior_no_show_flags is 1, but that is a lifetime counter and POL-GEN-01 forbids substituting it for the trailing-30-day field.

ruling.explanation:
Rider, the SGD 4.50 cancellation fee charged on this trip is refunded to you in full. Driver, no compensation is payable to you.

Why the fee does not stand. The charge can survive only if the driver held position inside the pickup geofence for the whole free waiting period of 180 seconds (trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec, zone class STANDARD). Measured as POL-NS-01(c) requires — from the first qualifying in-geofence GPS fix, and not from the 'arrived' tap — the driver's in-geofence hold ran from 10:43:10 to 10:45:40, a continuous run of 150 seconds carried by 16 qualifying fixes, and he cancelled at 10:45:43. That is 30 seconds short. POL-NS-06 therefore makes the fee not chargeable and refunds it in full, whether or not the rider was present and whether or not the rider replied. The same result follows from POL-NS-05(i) if the 10:41:10 arrival marker is treated as false and the waiting clock is recomputed from the first qualifying in-geofence fix: a corrected dwell of 150 seconds is still short of 180. The fare ledger charged SGD 4.50 (fare_breakdown.cancellation_fee and total_charged 4.50, payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00); that is the figure refunded.

Driver, your claims are answered together. Your point that the trip record carries an 'arrived' event at 10:41:10, a wait timer at 10:41:12 and a termination under RIDER_NO_SHOW (POL-NS-01(d)) is accepted as to those facts, and your own concession that the marker was pressed early is accepted, but limb (c) of POL-NS-01 fails on the 150-second dwell, so the fee is not chargeable. Your claim for SGD 3.60 (80% of the SGD 4.50 fee) under POL-NS-07 is rejected: that clause pays only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full, and it is not. Your claim that the rider's device sat about 739 metres from the pin for the whole window (46 fixes, zero speed, far outside the 100 m STANDARD rider-presence radius) is accepted, and your point that the rider sent no locating or coordinating message — so the rider-exonerating clause POL-NS-04 cannot fire — is also accepted; but the rider's absence does not save a fee that was collected before the waiting period was served, and the refund here does not depend on POL-NS-04 or on where the rider was. Your point that the fare line reconciles with platform_policy and shows no defect under POL-NS-08(d) is accepted; it is no answer to the short dwell. Your point that the POL-NS-09 escalation triggers are not engaged is accepted, and your reference to rider_profile.prior_no_show_flags is a context-only field under POL-GEN-01, correctly not used and not a ground of this ruling.

Rider, your claims are answered together. Your claim that the 'arrived' tap was false, that the dwelling clock must be recomputed from the first qualifying in-geofence fix at 10:43:10, and that the dwell of 150 seconds falls 30 seconds short of the 180-second minimum is accepted, and it decides the case: the full SGD 4.50 is refunded. Your supporting point that the driver's admission ('I pressed arrived a bit early') confirms an early marker is accepted, though the short dwell determines the outcome even without it. Your claim that the driver's track shows a mean distance of 2,647 metres and a maximum of 7,088 metres with speeds up to 47 kph is noted but not needed: those figures span the whole approach journey and do not by themselves fix his position at 10:41:10, and the dwell decides the case on its own. Your claim that the rider 'was present at the pickup' is rejected — a device sitting about 739 metres from the pin is not presence at the pickup; this rejection changes nothing, because the refund does not depend on rider presence. Your point that the driver's chat message at 10:41:30 does not cure the shortfall is accepted, as is your point that the fare ledger reconciles and the amount to be returned is the full SGD 4.50. Your point that the anti-farming check does not trip (driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 1 against 129 completed trips, a rate of 0.008, below the thresholds of 4 and 0.08) and that POL-NS-09(c) and (d) are not engaged (rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 0, and neither profile shows a counterparty dispute in 90 days) is accepted.

No escalation. This is not a case of two admissible artifacts in unresolvable conflict: the trip record's wait timer and the GPS trace's in-geofence run are reconciled by POL-NS-01(c) and POL-NS-05, which say from which fix the clock runs. No artifact carrying the deciding fact is impaired under POL-NS-08: the GPS trace has 100.0% coverage, 80 fixes, no gaps longer than 120 seconds and no clock skew over 90 seconds, the chat log's single message matches trip_record.chat_message_count, and the fare line reconciles. The traffic advisory is MISSING (weight 0.0) and carries nothing; it changes nothing here, because the trace contains a single in-geofence interval, so no accumulation under POL-NS-06(i) was possible in any event. The two advocate claims that cite that MISSING advisory without naming its MISSING_ARTIFACT issue code are discarded in the audit record, as POL-GEN-02(1) requires, and nothing in this ruling rests on that artifact.

Confidence is 0.92. The 150-second dwell is carried by EV-GPS-02750 and the 180-second requirement and cancellation time by EV-TRIP-02750, both at weight 1.0, so the cap is 1.0. The monetary effect is SGD 4.50, below the SGD 8.00 automatic execution threshold in POL-GEN-05, so the refund executes on issue. Both parties may appeal this provisional ruling once within 30 days under POL-GEN-04.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and the driver: the SGD 4.50 cancellation fee charged to the rider is refunded in full, and the driver receives no compensation.

Why the fee fails. A no-show fee needs all four POL-NS-01 limbs. The trip record (EV-TRIP-02750) does supply a driver 'arrived' event at 10:41:10 and a driver termination at 10:45:43 under reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW, which limb (d) recognises. Limb (c) none the less fails on the driver's own telemetry: the GPS trace (EV-GPS-02750) puts the driver's first qualifying in-geofence fix - accuracy-filtered and inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius - at 10:43:10, and his continuous hold inside the geofence runs 150 seconds, from 10:43:10 to 10:45:40, which is 30 seconds short of the 180-second free waiting period in force for this trip under trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec. POL-NS-01(c) measures the dwell from the first qualifying in-geofence fix, not from the 'arrived' tap, so the trip record's 4.5-minute wait figure and the 10:41:12 wait timer do not make the charge good. Limb (d) fails for the same reason: the 10:45:43 cancellation came before the required dwell would have completed at 10:46:10.

The arrival marker. The driver's own statement in the dispute record - 'I pressed arrived a bit early but I did wait at the pin' - concedes the 10:41:10 marker was early, and the trace bears it out: the first qualifying in-geofence fix is 120 seconds after the tap. On the POL-NS-05 recomputation the waiting clock runs from 10:43:10, the corrected dwell is 150 seconds, and POL-NS-05(i) refunds the fee in full with no compensation. POL-NS-06 gives the same result on its own terms: a 30-second shortfall against a 180-second minimum refunds the fee whether or not the rider was present or responsive. Because the driver did hold position inside the geofence for a qualifying run, POL-NS-05(ii)'s false-arrival referral is not produced - that limb applies only where no qualifying in-geofence fix exists anywhere in the trip, or where a false marker still leaves a dwell meeting the minimum - and no escalation arises under POL-NS-09: no admissible artifacts contradict each other unresolved (POL-NS-05 resolves the marker against the tap), no profile trigger fires, and no deciding fact rests on impaired evidence.

Driver's claims. The arrival and RIDER_NO_SHOW claims are accepted as far as they go but are outweighed by the limb (c) failure above. Your own figure - the 150-second qualifying in-geofence run - is accepted and is what decides the case. The rider-track points (46 fixes, 735-743 m from the pin, 0 kph; no rider locating message in the chat log) are accepted, and POL-NS-04 cannot exonerate the rider on them; but POL-NS-04 decides exoneration only, and POL-NS-06 refunds on the shortfall regardless, so they change nothing. For the same reason, and because the driver's stationary fixes lie inside the arrival radius rather than outside it within 400 m, POL-NS-03 does not apply. The claim to SGD 3.60 driver compensation is refused: POL-NS-07 pays only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full and no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displaces it, and POL-NS-06 displaces it. The anti-farming check was rightly not treated as tripped (1 no-show termination in 30 days against 129 completed trips), but it only matters where compensation is otherwise payable. The fare reconciliation is accepted: the SGD 4.50 cancellation-fee line equals platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd, so there is no POL-NS-08(d) defect and the full SGD 4.50 is refunded.

Rider's claims. The false-marker and 30-second-shortfall claims are accepted and decide the case. The submission that the rider was at the pickup is rejected: the rider's own track puts the device 735-743 m away throughout and stationary - although that finding does not affect the refund, which POL-NS-06 makes independent of rider presence. The driver's chat message at 10:41:30 does not cure the shortfall. The profile claims are accepted: no POL-NS-09(c) or (d) trigger fires, and prior_no_show_flags is properly not substituted for the 30-day counter.

Evidence weighting. ruling.explanation:
To both parties: the SGD 4.50 no-show cancellation fee on TRP-02750 is refunded to the rider in full.

A no-show fee is chargeable only if the driver held position inside the pickup geofence for the whole free waiting period in force. For this trip that period is 180 seconds (trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec, EV-TRIP-02750). The GPS trace (EV-GPS-02750) shows the driver's only in-geofence hold at the pin ran from 10:43:10 to 10:45:40 - 150 seconds, with 16 qualifying fixes - and he cancelled at 10:45:43. The dwell is measured from the first qualifying in-geofence fix (10:43:10) and not from the 'arrived' tap at 10:41:10, so the effective dwell is 150 seconds against the required 180: a 30-second shortfall. POL-NS-01(c) therefore fails, and POL-NS-06 refunds the cancellation-fee line in full, whether or not the rider was present and whether or not the rider responded to messages.

The arrival marker was pressed early: the driver's own statement ('I pressed arrived a bit early but I did wait at the pin') and the 120 seconds between the tap and the first in-geofence fix confirm it. Under POL-NS-05 the waiting clock restarts at 10:43:10; the corrected dwell of 150 seconds is still short, so POL-NS-05(i) gives the same result - full refund, no driver compensation.

Driver's points answered. The 'arrived' event, the wait timer and the RIDER_NO_SHOW reason code are on the record (EV-TRIP-02750), and limb (d) is satisfied in form, but a no-show fee needs all four limbs and limb (c) is not met. That the rider's own track places the rider about 740 m from the pin (46 fixes, stationary) and that the rider sent no locating or coordinating message are both accepted - POL-NS-04 cannot exonerate the rider - but rider presence is not what decides the fee, because POL-NS-06 refunds it either way. The fare ledger reconciles exactly (cancellation-fee line SGD 4.50 = platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd 4.50), so there is no POL-NS-08(d) defect. The claim to SGD 3.60 driver compensation under POL-NS-07 is refused: POL-NS-07 requires POL-NS-01 to be satisfied in full, and POL-NS-05 and POL-NS-06 displace it. The anti-farming check did not trip (driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d = 1; 1/129 is about 0.008), but clearing that check creates no entitlement by itself.

Rider's points answered. The false-arrival argument (marker at 10:41:10, first qualifying in-geofence fix at 10:43:10, corrected dwell 30 seconds short) is accepted and is decisive, as is the corroboration that the driver's mean distance across the trace was 2,647 m with speeds up to 47 kph while he was on the road network. The claim that the rider was present at the pickup is not accepted: the rider's own track places the rider roughly 740 m from the pin, outside the 100 m STANDARD rider-presence radius, and POL-NS-11 does not apply because that test could be run and failed - but this does not change the outcome, since the refund does not depend on the rider's presence. The fare reconciliation point is accepted.

No referral is added. POL-NS-05's false-arrival referral fires only where no qualifying in-geofence fix exists anywhere in the trip (limb ii) or where the corrected dwell still meets the minimum (limb iii); here the driver did reach the pin and the dwell fell short, which is limb (i), and no POL-NS-07 escalation packet is produced because the anti-farming check did not trip. No POL-NS-09 trigger fires, so the case is not escalated.

Weight and confidence: the deciding facts are carried by EV-GPS-02750 and EV-TRIP-02750, both at weight_multiplier 1.0, so the POL-GEN-02(2) cap is 1.0. The traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-02750-01 is MISSING (weight 0.0) and carries no deciding fact; it is only why POL-NS-06(i) accumulation across intervals is unavailable. The monetary effect (SGD 4.50) is below the POL-GEN-05 execution threshold of SGD 8.00, so it executes automatically.

ruling.explanation:
Rider and driver, this dispute is about the SGD 4.50 no-show cancellation fee charged on trip TRP-02750. The fee is refunded in full.

A no-show fee stands only if the driver actually held position at the pickup pin for the free waiting period in force, which the trip record puts at 180 seconds for this trip (EV-TRIP-02750, platform_policy.free_wait_sec; the pickup is STANDARD class, so the arrival radius is 50 m). The driver tapped 'arrived' at 10:41:10, but the GPS trace (EV-GPS-02750) shows no qualifying fix inside that radius at that moment - his first qualifying in-geofence fix is at 10:43:10, 120 seconds later - and the driver's own statement ('I pressed arrived a bit early but I did wait at the pin') concedes the early tap. The marker therefore does not start the waiting clock, and both POL-NS-01(c) and POL-NS-05 measure the dwell from the first qualifying in-geofence fix. On the trace the driver's one continuous hold inside the radius ran 150 seconds, from 10:43:10 to 10:45:40, and he cancelled at 10:45:43 - 30 seconds short of the 180 seconds required.

That shortfall is decisive. POL-NS-06 refunds the cancellation fee in full where the effective in-geofence dwell is shorter than the free waiting period, whether or not the rider was present and whether or not the rider responded; POL-NS-05(i) reaches the same result on the recomputed clock. The one route that could have added time - accumulation under POL-NS-06(i) - is unavailable here: the trace shows a single in-geofence interval, and the traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-02750-01) is MISSING at weight 0.0, which makes that limb unavailable rather than exonerating anyone.

No driver compensation is payable. POL-NS-07 pays only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full, and limb (c) fails on the dwell; POL-NS-05(i) says expressly that no compensation is payable on this outcome. The driver's claim for SGD 3.60 (80 per cent of SGD 4.50, the figure computed in EV-FARE-02750) is rejected for that reason. The anti-farming check does not trip (driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 1 against 129 completed trips in 30 days), so POL-NS-09 does not escalate on that ground, and no other escalation trigger is engaged: the driver's profile counters relied on are trailing-30-day figures, not lifetime counters.

On the parties' other points: the driver is right that the chat log (EV-CHAT-02750) holds no rider message and that the rider's own track places the rider 735-743 m from the pin, but neither helps him - the refund under POL-NS-06 does not depend on the rider's presence, and POL-NS-04 cannot fire without a rider locating message (limb (a)). The rider's assertion that his own track shows him 'present at the pickup' is rejected: 739 m from the pin is not at the pin, and the track shows only that his device was stationary throughout. The rider's wider point - that the app reported an arrival that had not happened - is accepted and is the basis of this ruling.

Amount and execution: the fare ledger (EV-FARE-02750) shows SGD 4.50 charged, matching platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd, with no refund issued. The full SGD 4.50 cancellation-fee line is refunded, with nothing added for booking, platform or waiting charges. The monetary effect, SGD 4.50, is below the SGD 8.00 automatic execution threshold (POL-GEN-05), so it executes on issue.

Confidence is 0.95. The deciding measurement - the 150-second dwell - is carried by the GPS trace (EV-GPS-02750) at weight 1.0, so the POL-GEN-02 cap is 1.0; the missing advisory at weight 0.0 carries no fact and does not lower that cap, the fare ledger reconciles with the policy figure so no POL-NS-08(d) defect arises, and the record shows no clock skew, trace gap or chat truncation that would engage POL-NS-08 or POL-NS-09(e).

No referral is issued. The false-arrival referral in POL-NS-05(ii) applies only where no qualifying in-geofence fix exists anywhere in the trip, and the referral in POL-NS-05(iii) only where the corrected dwell meets the minimum; this case has a qualifying 150-second hold that fell short of the required 180 seconds, so neither limb applies and no clause directs a referral.

But POL-NS-05(iii) is explicit that a false marker does not by itself defeat the fee where the corrected dwell still meets the minimum, and the corrected dwell here is 150 seconds against a STANDARD minimum of 180 seconds — so this concession is real and it costs the driver the fee.
